Ability scores will not be automatically altered other than their tool tips (mouseover texts) and in the Scores dialog.

tooltip:
Type (or select) the name of the race you want to have on this page. Note that first a list of player races is given, followed by an alphabetical list of creatures. You are not limited by the names in the list. Just typing "Drow" will also be recognized, for example.

𝙎𝙚𝙡𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙖 𝙘𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙩𝙪𝙧𝙚
All information of the creature will automatically be added. This includes ability scores, proficiencies, senses, weapons, etc. You can change the things afterwards.
Because not all creatures need the same amount of space for all their feature text,some fields may overflow. You can manually edit these fields so that everything is visible when printed (e.g. move things to the "Noted" below).

𝙎𝙚𝙡𝙚𝙘𝙩𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙖 𝙥𝙡𝙖𝙮𝙚𝙧 𝙧𝙖𝙘𝙚
All the same things as selecting a player race on the first page will happen, with the exception that no limited feature or ability DC is added as there is no room for that.

𝘾𝙝𝙖𝙣𝙜𝙞𝙣𝙜 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙧𝙖𝙘𝙚
If you entered a race that was recognized and then change the entry to something that is not recognized, all the features and abilities of the recognized race will remain in place. This way, you can change the name of the race to something, while keeping the stats of something else. For example, you can choose "Frog" and then change it to "Salamander", creating a salamander with the stats of a frog.

Type (or select) the name of the creature you want to calculate a Wild Shape for.

𝙉𝙤𝙩 𝙖𝙪𝙩𝙤-𝙪𝙥𝙙𝙖𝙩𝙚𝙙
The generated stats will not auto-update once you change something on the first page! They will only update when your druid level changes. You can have them re-calculated using the "Wild Shape Options" button at the top of this page.

𝙁𝙞𝙧𝙨𝙩 𝙘𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙩𝙚 𝙩𝙝𝙚 𝙘𝙝𝙖𝙧𝙖𝙘𝙩𝙚𝙧
Note that nothing will happen if no character is defined on the 1st page.

𝘾𝙖𝙡𝙘𝙪𝙡𝙖𝙩𝙞𝙤𝙣 𝙞𝙨 𝙬𝙧𝙤𝙣𝙜
The Wild Shape rules are open for interpertation and your DM might not approve with the way it is done here. You can change the calculation of proficiencies using the "Wild Shape Options" button at the top of this page.
You can always change the outcome yourself, because all of the fields are editable.

Different, setting-dependent race names are recognized as well. For example, typing "Moon Elf" will result in all the traits and features of the "High Elf" from the Player's Handbook.

Type the name of the armor (or select it from the drop-down menu) and its AC and features will be filled out automatically, provided that its a recognized armor.

𝘼𝙡𝙩𝙚𝙧𝙣𝙖𝙩𝙞𝙫𝙚 𝙨𝙥𝙚𝙡𝙡𝙞𝙣𝙜
You can use alternative spellings, descriptions and embellishments. For example: "Golden Breastplate of Lathander" will result in the AC and attributes of a "Breastplate".

𝙐𝙣𝙖𝙧𝙢𝙤𝙧𝙚𝙙 𝘿𝙚𝙛𝙚𝙣𝙨𝙚
Using either "unarmored", "naked", "nothing", or "no armor" combined with an abbreviation of one of the six ability scores will result in the armor being calculated with that ability score. For example: "Unarmored Defense (Int)".
If you do not include the abbreviation, the sheet will auto-fill an armor AC of 10.

𝙈𝙖𝙜𝙞𝙘 𝙗𝙤𝙣𝙪𝙨
Any magical bonus you type in this field is added to the AC of the armor type. For example: "Chain mail +1" or "Plate -2".
